That's the lowest level of support since 1995.Last year, more than 160 countries backed the proposal. Germany, Italy and Latvia abstained for the first time in 34 years.Several countries, including Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Morocco, Slovenia and Bosnia, voted against the resolution, many for the first time.The resolution, while not legally binding, is seen as a reflection of international opinion. John Healey quit as U.K. defense secretary in the dying days of Keir Starmer's government in a row over funding. On Wednesday he gave his first budget as chancellor under new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, setting out the government's tax and spending plans. Healey committed for the first time to spending 3% of GDP on the nation's defenses by 2030 — something he had called for when he quit Starmer's administration. But he declined to say where he would find the money, a staging post on the way to meeting NATO's target of 3.5% of GDP by 2035. Instead, he said a broader review of government spending would address it next year.
